summary.intent: Execute Phase 50 (IPFS/IPNS Data-Integrity Fixes) end-to-end via the GSD manager, resolving Phase 42 unpin-integrity findings and unenroll-subtrees bug, then ship via PR.
summary.outcome: All 5 plans executed in parallel worktrees, code-review blockers fixed (cycle guard, .catch, TOCTOU/lock races), phase verified 3/3 must-haves, simplified, security-reviewed (0 exploitable findings), and shipped as PR #527.

repo: pnpm/orval in worktrees resolve workspace root to the main checkout (no per-worktree node_modules), so api:generate and installs inside a worktree leak 132 api-client files into the orchestrator working tree as uncommitted changes — must discard before merge
Husky regenerates .husky/_/* stubs (untracked) when pnpm install/api:generate runs inside a worktree; these block cleanup-wave's dirty-tree check and must be cleaned before merge

cleanup-wave helper reports opaque 'merge_failed' with empty stderr when its internal merge commit is blocked by a slow pre-commit hook (lint-staged across 137 generated files); the git merge itself is already applied and can be completed manually
The gsd commit helper has a known false-negative: it reports 'commit_failed' but the commit actually lands — always verify with git log before retrying
PR title must use Conventional Commits format without parens; pr-title.yml CI rejects 'Phase 50: IPFS/IPNS Data-Integrity Fixes' — use 'fix: ...' instead
gh CLI in this repo requires 'env -u GITHUB_TOKEN'; fetch+rebase needed after 'gh pr create' because the release-please bot lands a commit on PR open
The dep-string parser misreads 'Phase 49 (v1.1 baseline)' as a phantom dependency 'phase 1.1', reporting unsatisfied deps even when Phase 49 is complete — workaround: confirm real dep manually
todos/done (70 items) was a legacy folder; GSD tooling exclusively references todos/completed — drift had accumulated since ~Jun 15 update, needed one-time consolidation

50-REVIEW.md documents findings in their pre-fix state; after fixes are applied in later commits, the REVIEW.md and VERIFICATION.md appear contradictory — add a resolution table to REVIEW.md to reconcile

code.finding: collectSubtreeIpnsNamesAsync had no visited Set, allowing A->B->A folder-metadata cycles (client-influenced data) to overflow the stack. ensureFolderLoaded (line 549) and the shared walker (line 2526) both had cycle guards — this method's docstring claimed to mirror that pattern but didn't. Fixed by adding visited Set param at line 286, guard at 293-294.

4 fire-and-forget unenroll dispatch sites (emptyBin, purge, deleteItem, permanentDelete) had no .catch(), violating the 'failures never block the caller' contract and causing unhandled promise rejections. Consolidated into fireAndForgetUnenrollEntries helper by /simplify which owns the .catch.

abs(int4) in pg_advisory_xact_lock(abs(hashtext($1))::bigint) overflows for INT_MIN (-2147483648), making that CID permanently undeletable. Dropped abs() — pg_advisory_xact_lock accepts signed bigint and int4 sign-extends safely.

Drain re-checked pinnedCidRepository.count and called unpinFile in autocommit with no advisory lock — TOCTOU window where concurrent re-upload inserts a fresh pinned_cids row after drain reads count=0, causing physical unpin of a live CID (data loss). Fixed: wrap recheck+unpin+delete in a transaction that first takes the same pg_advisory_xact_lock used by guardedUnpin.

A comment 'renamed from outboxRowInserted' remained after the IN-06 rename to shouldAttemptPhysicalUnpin. VALIDATION.md grep for 'outboxRowInserted' was too broad and hit the comment, producing a false-positive assertion failure. The actual variable is correctly renamed.

pendingUnpinRepository.delete in guardedUnpin ran after the advisory-lock transaction released, unserialized against concurrent guardedUnpin/drain that could re-insert the outbox row. Fixed: re-take advisory lock in a short post-commit transaction and delete through manager-scoped repo.

workflow: When cleanup-wave fails mid-run (some worktrees merged, others not), re-run cleanup only for the remaining worktrees — the helper is not idempotent on already-removed worktrees
Post-merge gate should use targeted test suites (changed files only) rather than full parallel monorepo suite to avoid RAM starvation and infra-dependent integration tests
Orphan worktree-agent-* branches from prior sessions accumulate but are safe to leave — verify no attached worktrees before touching them

cleanup-wave's STATE.md write (state.begin-phase) makes the orchestrator tree dirty, which can block the helper's subsequent merge step — the workaround is completing the merge manually when this happens
CodeRabbit CLI (v0.6.1) with --agent flag produces structured findings; doc-consistency issues (pre-fix REVIEW.md vs post-fix VERIFICATION.md) show up as 'critical' but are not code bugs

friction: cleanup-wave reported opaque 'merge_failed' with empty stderr on 50-05 — took multiple diagnostic rounds to identify the pre-commit hook (lint-staged across 137 generated files) as the silent blocker

pnpm/orval workspace-root resolution leaked 132 api-client files + client.ts into the orchestrator working tree, blocking the re-run of cleanup-wave and requiring manual verification that leaked files matched the worktree before discarding
Husky .husky/_/* stubs left untracked in 50-05 worktree caused the first cleanup-wave pass to bail before attempting the merge
Dep-string parser created a phantom 'phase 1.1' dependency, surfacing a false 'deps unsatisfied' warning that had to be diagnosed before dispatching execution
gsd commit helper false-negative forced a git log verification after every tracking commit to confirm the commit actually landed
todos/done vs todos/completed drift required an unplanned 70-file consolidation mid-session to keep tooling aligned
